# package canopen

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-otfp/protocols/canopen"
```

Package canopen fingerprints CANopen gateways that expose a CANopen network through the CiA 309-3 ASCII command interface over TCP, such as CANopenNode's canopend ("-c tcp-\<port>") and CANopen-Ethernet gateways.

CiA 309-3 commands are text lines "\[\<sequence>] \[\[\<net>] \<node>] \<command>" answered by "\[\<sequence>] OK", "\[\<sequence>] \<value>" or "\[\<sequence>] ERROR:\<code>", where the code is a gateway error (100..999) or a 32-bit SDO abort code (0xhhhhhhhh).

Detection sends the gateway management service "info version" (Get version) with a random sequence number. The gateway answers it itself, without any CAN traffic: with its version record (vendor-ID, product code, revision, serial number, gateway class, protocol version, implementation class), or with "ERROR:100" (request not supported) as CANopenNode does. Only a strict 309-3 response line that echoes the sequence number is accepted; banners of HTTP, SSH, SMTP and other text services, echoes of the probe and binary data are rejected.

Identify mode, when the scan allows read-only probes, additionally reads the identity of one CANopen node through the gateway's SDO client: the device type (0x1000), the manufacturer device name (0x1008), the software version (0x100A) and the identity object (0x1018 sub 1..4). These are SDO uploads on the CAN bus. They go to the gateway's default node, or to the node named in Config.Node. Nothing is ever written.
